Parent.title: Parent
Parent.description: Represents a parent involved in the co-parenting arrangement.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Parent entity.

email.description: The email address of the parent.

ChildSupportPayment.title: ChildSupportPayment
ChildSupportPayment.description: Represents a monthly child support payment.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Child Support Payment entity.

payerId.description: Reference to the Parent who is paying the child support. (Relationship: Parent 1:N ChildSupportPayment)

amount.description: The amount of the child support payment.

paymentDate.description: The date the child support payment was made.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Expense entity.

date.description: The date the expense was incurred.

parentPayerId.description: Reference to the Parent who paid for the expense. (Relationship: Parent 1:N Expense)

ExpenseCoverage.title: ExpenseCoverage
ExpenseCoverage.description: Represents the expense coverage percentage for each parent.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Expense Coverage entity.

parentId.description: Reference to the Parent to whom this percentage applies. (Relationship: Parent 1:N ExpenseCoverage)

coveragePercentage.description: The percentage of expense coverage for this parent (e.g., 0.5 for 50%).

month.description: The month this coverage percentage applies to. Represented as a number (1-12)

year.description: The year this coverage percentage applies to.

MonthlyReport.title: MonthlyReport
MonthlyReport.description: Represents a monthly report containing child support and expense information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Monthly Report entity.

definition.description: Stores parent profiles. The `parentId` parameter corresponds to the user's UID. All data related to a specific parent will reside under this document.

params.name: parentId
params.description: The unique ID of the parent, matching the Firebase Auth UID.

definition.description: Stores child support payments made by a parent. Includes `payerId` which is equal to the parentId and ensures that the parent can only access payments they made.

params.name: parentId
params.description: The unique ID of the parent making the payment.

params.name: childSupportPaymentId
params.description: The unique ID of the child support payment.

definition.description: Stores expenses logged by a parent. Includes `parentPayerId` which is equal to the parentId and ensures that the parent can only access expenses they created.

params.name: parentId
params.description: The unique ID of the parent who paid for the expense.

params.name: expenseId
params.description: The unique ID of the expense.

definition.description: Stores expense coverage percentages for a parent for a specific month and year. Includes `parentId` to define the parent to whom the coverage applies.

params.name: parentId
params.description: The unique ID of the parent to whom the coverage applies.

params.name: expenseCoverageId
params.description: The unique ID of the expense coverage setting.

definition.description: Stores monthly reports generated for a parent. Reports reference child support payments and expenses for the month.  The report is tied to a specific parent by the parentId parameter.

params.name: parentId
params.description: The unique ID of the parent for whom the report is generated.

params.name: monthlyReportId
params.description: The unique ID of the monthly report.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support a co-parenting finance application, focusing on child support payments, expense tracking, coverage percentages, and monthly reports. The structure prioritizes authorization independence and efficient data retrieval.

**Authorization Independence:**

*   **Parents Collection:** Each parent has their own document in the `/parents` collection.
*   **Parent Owned Data:** All child support payments, expenses, expense coverages, and monthly reports are stored as subcollections under the parent's document (`/parents/{parentId}`). This ensures that access control is based on the current user's ID (`request.auth.uid`) matching the `parentId` or relevant ownership fields in the subcollections, eliminating the need for `get()` calls to parent documents.

**Structural Segregation:**

*   Expenses, ChildSupportPayments, ExpenseCoverage settings, and MonthlyReports are segregated into their own collections. This allows for consistent security rules at each level.

**Access Modeling:**

*   **Path-Based Ownership:** The structure heavily relies on path-based ownership. For example, expenses are stored under `/parents/{parentId}/expenses/{expenseId}`, ensuring that only the parent who created the expense has access to it.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**

*   The segregation of data into separate collections, combined with path-based ownership, enables secure list operations. Rules can efficiently check if `request.auth.uid` matches the `parentId` without needing to filter based on document content. The denormalization of the `parentId` into the subcollection documents also allows for secure and efficient querying.

**Invariants:**

*   Path-based ownership enforces the invariant that only a parent can create, modify, or delete data under their own node. The `parentId` field in subcollections is immutable, further reinforcing ownership integrity.

This structure ensures that security rules are simple, robust, and easily debuggable, adhering to the core design principles.
